title: Literature review: inverted and suspended-occupant tolerance
context: RideBelt is an open, safety-critical Hee-Lee Oss project: an optional rider-worn backup restraint (low hip belt + short tethers; optional clip-on Shoulder Module or one-piece Integrated Harness) that latches into an open seat anchor standard (RAS). ALL safety content is DRAFT and not for use until a credentialed engineer signs off at the MVP gate (GOVERNANCE.md). Never remove a DRAFT banner, never give instructions for wearing or attaching anything to a ride, never copy text from paid standards (cite by number and title only), never name private individuals or incident victims, and respect the patent design-arounds in docs/research/patentability-fto.md. REQ-H5 covers riders held upside down when a ride stops. Literature on suspension trauma (harness hang), inverted vehicle occupants and ride stoppages gives tolerance data.
objective: Summarise what is known about tolerance to prolonged inverted or suspended restraint (time limits, symptoms, risk factors, rescue priorities), with sources.
acceptanceCriteria: Distinguishes upright harness suspension from inverted seated restraint
Ends with candidate inputs for REQ-H5, labelled for engineer review
Every factual claim has a cited, working source link; estimates are labelled as estimates
